claim_boundary: This is a characteristic-zero literal-intersection zero theorem using the established exact iterated product-shadow theorem. It gives no new exact Chow rank or border-rank result. The pair boundary n=m^2-m, the cubic exceptional rows, shifted equality cases not already covered by the parent simplex theorem, and (q-1)n>=m^2 remain open. Literature novelty is not established.

theorem.initial_tiers: With r=m-1: F(1)=r^2; F(b)=r(r+1) for 2<=b<=r+1; F(r+2)=r(r+2), hence F(b)>=r(r+2) for b>=r+2.
theorem.pair_corollary: For m>=4 and m<=n<=m^2-m-1, every two-term Chow block is permanent-relative zero in output degree m.
theorem.private_dimension: If delta=m^2-(q-1)n>0 and a nonzero intersection survives, some private polar space in D_(m-1)(perm_n) has dimension at least delta.
theorem.q_ge_3_corollary: For m>=4,q>=3,(q-1)n<m^2, every q-term Chow block is permanent-relative zero.
theorem.shadow_criterion: Such an intersection is impossible whenever F^(m-2)_(n,m-1)(delta)>n.
